transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical support, my name is Connor. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Connor. My Hub 5 router is constantly dropping the internet every thirty minutes, and when I touched it earlier it was burning hot to the touch and the top light is flashing red!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating it is when your broadband connection keeps dropping out while you are trying to work, Matthew. Let's look into the router status right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Connor, I have client video presentations this afternoon so I really need stability.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access the hardware telemetry, Matthew, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the address is 8 The Copse, Guildford, GU1 2TY, and my security PIN is 3391.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Matthew. I have your Hub 5 connection open on our diagnostic portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to make sure I understand the situation clearly: your Hub 5 is turning extremely hot to the touch, the top LED is flashing solid red, and your Wi-Fi signal drops every thirty minutes since moving the equipment. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what is happening. The casing feels almost like a hot radiator.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where exactly is the router placed inside your home right now? Is it positioned on an open tabletop, and are the side ventilation grilles clear of obstructions?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, two days ago my wife and I tidied up the living room, so we placed the router inside our wooden TV media console cabinet and closed the wooden doors to hide the ugly black power bricks and wires.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are there any ventilation cut-outs or cooling fans installed on the rear panels of that TV cabinet?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it's a solid English oak sideboard unit with magnetic wooden doors and only a small circular two-inch hole cut at the back where the black power cables pass through.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other heat-generating equipment located inside that cabinet alongside the Hub 5?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our Sky television set-top box and a PlayStation 5 console are also stacked right next to it on the same wooden shelf.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Electronics stacked closely inside an unventilated solid oak cabinet trap ambient thermal dissipation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I thought modern broadband routers were engineered with heavy aluminum heatsinks specifically designed to run coolly inside domestic living room storage furniture without needing active fans.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub 5 houses an internal Broadcom Docsis 3.1 chipset and Wi-Fi 6 multi-gigabit radio power amplifiers that consume up to twenty-eight watts of continuous electrical power, generating substantial heat.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean the persistent red flashing light indicates thermal protection CPU throttling?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, when internal silicon core temperatures exceed eighty-five degrees Celsius, the firmware throttles the CPU clock speed and disconnects radio channels to prevent fire or silicon burnout.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why the Wi-Fi drops every thirty minutes when it gets too hot.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about thirty-five seconds while I query the hardware telemetry logs for your modem's thermal history.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Matthew. The remote log records twelve emergency thermal shutdown events over the past forty-eight hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you dispatch an engineer with a replacement Hub 5 today just in case the motherboard has suffered permanent heat degradation?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, if you put a hot electronic box inside a wooden cupboard with no vents, obviously it's going to cook itself, Matthew. What did you expect to happen?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is absolutely no need to take that rude and patronizing tone with me, Connor! I am an accountant, not a network engineer, and the installation booklet never warned against putting it in a cabinet!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our user guide explicitly states that broadband hubs require at least four inches of open airspace on all sides.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am asking if the hardware has suffered permanent thermal damage, because I cannot afford dropped calls during tax audit presentations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our warranty terms do not cover replacement routers when thermal overheating is caused by customer placement in enclosed furniture. Every subscriber agrees to terms stating that electronic equipment must be operated in well-ventilated ambient environments.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you are refusing to replace the router even if the internal capacitors have been damaged by the heat?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will have to remove the hub from the cabinet immediately, place it out on an elevated open surface, and monitor it yourself over the weekend.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should I do if the unit continues to drop connections even while sitting out in the open room?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If it drops while in open air after forty-eight hours of normal operation, only then will our warranty desk consider opening an RMA hardware return ticket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least run an active signal-to-noise ratio check on our physical street coaxial line right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I checked the physical downstream power levels while querying the telemetry; the street signal levels on your coax feed are within standard tolerances at plus two dBmV.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about the upstream transmit power margin?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Upstream transmit power is sitting at forty-three dBmV across four bonded channels, which is completely normal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the street connection itself is completely healthy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The street infrastructure is flawless; the root fault is exclusively local thermal dissipation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will pull the hub out of the TV sideboard right now onto the open wooden desk next to the window.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Make sure both the side vents and the bottom intake slots have unrestricted air clearance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm setting it upright on its integrated stand with nothing within twelve inches of it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The casing will take approximately twenty minutes to dissipate retained internal heat down to standard operating temperatures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I unplug the power cord to reboot the internal thermal sensors?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Power cycle the unit for sixty seconds once the plastic casing feels cool to the touch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will force a clean firmware cold boot.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And ensure that the Sky box and PlayStation inside that TV unit are also ventilated, or their cooling fans will blow hot exhaust directly onto each other.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will keep the cabinet doors permanently open whenever those devices are switched on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, Matthew, this TV console is located in your ground floor living room?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, right on the open oak desk in the ground floor living room.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That location will also improve your 5GHz Wi-Fi beamforming propagation across the ground floor area.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Wi-Fi signal in the kitchen was slightly weak before, so improved coverage will be very welcome.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Elevated placement away from dense wooden cabinet panels significantly reduces radio frequency attenuation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have sixty megabytes broadband speed when it is working properly, which is plenty for our daily needs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your current subscription tier is Superfast 100, which delivers one hundred and eight megabits downstream.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, one hundred megabits downstream, sorry, my mistake.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Connor, if the light stays flashing amber or red after cooling down for twenty minutes, what exact number should I call?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just pull it out onto the table and see what happens. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Matthew. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Connor, what is the direct number... hello?
